questions.stem: Which statement about the onset of chronic inflammation is correct?

options.A: It can occur de novo, with no acute phase
options.B: It requires a failed acute reaction first
options.C: It cannot follow repeated bouts of acute inflammation
options.E: It begins when neutrophils undergo apoptosis

questions.explanation: Chronic inflammation can follow persistent or recurrent injury or an ineffective response, and it can also occur de novo. B: It can occur de novo. C: Repeated acute bouts are a listed cause. D: Infection is one of several etiologies. E: Neutrophil apoptosis is part of resolution.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes chronic nonspecific inflammation from acute inflammation?

options.C: Infiltration of leukocytes
options.E: Exudation of protein-rich fluid into tissue

questions.explanation: Chronic nonspecific inflammation shows mononuclear cells, tissue destruction with concomitant repair (new vessels, fibroblasts, fibrosis), and architectural distortion. B: Increased permeability is a hallmark of acute inflammation. C: Leukocyte infiltration occurs in both. D: Mediators act in both. E: Exudation is a hallmark of acute inflammation.

questions.stem: In chronic inflammation, which statement about the macrophage–lymphocyte interaction is correct?

options.B: Macrophages inhibit lymphocytes to limit the response
options.C: Plasma cells arise from activated T lymphocytes in the tissue
options.D: Monocytes enter the tissue without chemotactic signals
options.E: Neutrophils present antigen to B lymphocytes

questions.explanation: Monocytes are recruited by chemotactic factors; macrophage cytokines activate lymphocytes, which in turn release cytokines that activate macrophages; B cells activated by macrophage-presented antigen become plasma cells. B: Macrophages activate lymphocytes. C: Plasma cells come from B cells. D: Chemotactic factors recruit monocytes. E: Macrophages present the antigen.

questions.stem: Which etiology of chronic inflammation is matched with the example given in the notes?

options.C: Repeated acute bouts – gallstone cholecystitis
options.E: Prolonged toxic exposure – peptic ulcer

questions.explanation: Chronic cholecystitis due to gallstones is the example of repeated bouts of acute inflammation. A: Gallstone cholecystitis is the repeated-bouts example. B: Asthma is an allergic example. D: Sarcoidosis is granulomatous with unknown cause. E: Peptic ulcer is not given as the toxic example.

questions.stem: Which statement about granulomas is correct?

options.A: Giant cells form from fusion of epithelioid macrophages
options.B: Epithelioid cells are modified surface epithelial cells
options.C: Granulomas are surrounded by a rim of neutrophils
options.D: Giant cells form from fusion of lymphocytes
options.E: Granulomas are made mainly of plasma cells

questions.explanation: Granulomas are nodular collections of epithelioid cells (specialized macrophages) with a lymphocyte rim; giant cells form by fusion of macrophages. B: Epithelioid cells are specialized macrophages. C: The rim is lymphocytes. D: Giant cells come from macrophages. E: Plasma cells are not the main cells.

questions.stem: Which statement about giant cells is correct?

options.A: Langhans giant cells are specific for tuberculosis
options.B: Foreign-body giant cells have nuclei scattered in the cytoplasm
options.C: Foreign-body giant cells have a peripheral horseshoe of nuclei
options.D: Megakaryocytes are pathologic giant cells of granulomas
options.E: Giant cells in herpes come from macrophage fusion

questions.explanation: Foreign-body giant cells have scattered nuclei; Langhans cells have peripheral horseshoe nuclei and are characteristic of, but not specific for, TB. A: Langhans cells are not TB-specific. C: The horseshoe pattern belongs to Langhans cells. D: The notes list megakaryocytes and osteoclasts as normal multinucleated cells. E: Herpes giant cells are infected epithelial cells.

questions.stem: A lymph node biopsy from a patient with fever and cough shows granulomas with central cheese-like necrosis. Which statement about this necrosis is correct?

options.A: It is liquefactive necrosis caused by pyogenic staphylococci
options.B: It is typical of the non-caseating granulomas of sarcoidosis
options.C: It results from T cells killing mycobacteria-laden macrophages
options.D: It results from neutrophil elastase digesting the node
options.E: It is coagulative necrosis from vascular occlusion

questions.explanation: Caseating granulomas are characteristic of TB; caseous necrosis results from T-cell killing of mycobacteria-laden macrophages and from free-radical injury. A: Liquefactive necrosis by pyogenic bacteria produces abscesses. B: Sarcoidosis granulomas are non-caseating. D: Elastase injury is not the mechanism described. E: Ischemic necrosis is not the mechanism in TB.

questions.stem: How does granuloma formation begin?

options.A: Neutrophils present antigen to CD8+ T cells
options.B: B cells present antigen to macrophages
options.C: Macrophages present antigen to CD4+ T cells
options.D: CD8+ T cells kill macrophages, releasing IFN-γ
options.E: Epithelioid cells release IL-1 to recruit T cells

questions.explanation: Poorly digestible antigen is presented by macrophages to CD4+ T cells; T-cell activation releases cytokines (especially IFN-γ) that transform macrophages into epithelioid and giant cells. A: Neutrophils are not the presenting cells. B: Macrophages present to T cells. D: The T cells involved are CD4+, and IFN-γ is released by activated T cells. E: Epithelioid cells are the result, not the starting signal.

questions.stem: Which statement about the etiology of granulomatous inflammation is correct?

options.A: Caseating granulomas are typical of autoimmune diseases
options.B: Sarcoidosis is the prototype of non-caseating granulomas
options.C: Crohn disease is listed as an infectious cause
options.D: Reactions to tumors produce abscesses rather than granulomas
options.E: Cat-scratch disease is caused by a fungus

questions.explanation: Non-caseating granulomas occur in several chronic inflammatory and autoimmune diseases; the prototype is sarcoidosis. A: Autoimmune diseases give non-caseating granulomas. C: Crohn disease is listed under unknown or autoimmune causes. D: Reaction to tumors is a listed cause. E: Cat-scratch disease is caused by a bacterium.

questions.stem: All of the following are listed as infectious causes of granulomatous inflammation EXCEPT:

options.C: Coccidioides immitis
options.E: Blastomyces dermatitidis

questions.explanation: Infectious causes listed are mycobacteria (M. tuberculosis, M. leprae), fungi (Blastomyces, Histoplasma, Coccidioides), T. pallidum and the cat-scratch bacterium. Staphylococci cause purulent inflammation and abscesses. A: M. leprae is listed. C: Coccidioides is listed. D: T. pallidum is listed. E: Blastomyces is listed.

questions.stem: Which statement about multinucleated cells is correct?

options.A: They are restricted to granulomatous lesions
options.C: They may be seen in virus-infected epithelial cells
options.E: They do not occur in tumors or in viral infections

questions.explanation: Multinucleated giant cells also occur in virus-infected cells (epithelial cells in herpes) and in some tumors; osteoclasts are normal multinucleated cells. A: They also occur outside granulomas. B: Osteoclasts are normal. D: Neutrophils are not multinucleated. E: Some tumors contain them.

questions.stem: When eosinophils are prominent in chronic inflammation, which etiology is most likely?

options.C: A parasitic or allergic cause
options.E: A pyogenic bacterial infection

questions.explanation: When chronic inflammation is due to parasites or allergic disorders, eosinophils are involved and seen at the site. A: Gallstone cholecystitis shows mononuclear cells. B: Foreign bodies cause granulomas with giant cells. D: Mycobacteria cause caseating granulomas. E: Pyogenic bacteria cause purulent inflammation.

questions.stem: Chronic inflammation occurs in which two major patterns?

options.C: Caseating and non-caseating granulomatous
options.E: Nonspecific and purulent

questions.explanation: Chronic inflammation occurs as chronic nonspecific inflammation and granulomatous inflammation. A: These are acute patterns. B: These are acute outcomes and patterns. C: These are the two granuloma types. E: Purulent is an acute pattern.

questions.stem: In chronic inflammation, antibody-producing plasma cells arise from:

options.A: T lymphocytes activated by macrophage cytokines
options.C: B lymphocytes activated by neutrophil-presented antigen
options.D: B lymphocytes activated by macrophage-presented antigen
options.E: Epithelioid cells activated by IFN-γ

questions.explanation: B lymphocyte activation by macrophage-presented antigen forms antibody-producing plasma cells. A: T cells do not become plasma cells. B: Monocytes become macrophages. C: Macrophages, not neutrophils, present the antigen. E: Epithelioid cells are modified macrophages.

questions.stem: Whenever a granuloma is found in a biopsy, which disease should always be excluded?

options.C: Crohn disease
options.E: Tuberculosis

questions.explanation: The notes state that in the presence of a granuloma, tuberculosis should always be excluded. A: Sarcoidosis is not the disease named for exclusion. B: Histoplasmosis is a cause, but TB is the one named. C: Crohn disease is a cause, but TB is the one named. D: Syphilis is a cause, but TB is the one named.

questions.stem: Which cytokine transforms monocytes and macrophages into epithelioid and giant cells?

options.C: Interleukin-1
options.E: Histamine

questions.explanation: Activated CD4+ T cells release cytokines, especially IFN-γ, which transform monocytes and macrophages into epithelioid and giant cells. A: TNF is not the cytokine named for this transformation. C: IL-1 drives systemic acute-phase effects. D: IL-8 is a neutrophil chemokine. E: Histamine is a vasoactive amine.

questions.stem: Which group lists only the fungi named as causes of granulomatous inflammation?

options.C: Blastomyces, Candida, Histoplasma
options.E: Histoplasma, M. leprae, Blastomyces

questions.explanation: The fungi listed are Blastomyces dermatitidis, Histoplasma capsulatum and Coccidioides immitis. A: Treponema is a bacterium. C: Candida is not in the list. D: Aspergillus is not in the list. E: M. leprae is a mycobacterium.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a normal multinucleated cell?

options.C: Neutrophil
options.E: Monocyte

questions.explanation: The notes name megakaryocytes and osteoclasts as normal multinucleated cells. (Standard sources describe megakaryocytes as polyploid with a single multilobed nucleus.) A: Plasma cells have one nucleus. B: Epithelioid cells have one nucleus but can fuse into giant cells. C: Neutrophils have one multilobed nucleus. E: Monocytes have one indented nucleus.

questions.stem: A granuloma contains giant cells whose nuclei form a horseshoe around the periphery. Which statement is correct?

options.A: These are foreign-body cells, specific for retained sutures
options.B: These are Langhans cells, specific for tuberculosis
options.C: These are foreign-body cells, formed from lymphocytes
options.D: These are virus-infected epithelial cells of herpes
options.E: These are Langhans cells, characteristic but not specific for TB

questions.explanation: Langhans giant cells have nuclei in a horseshoe at the periphery and are characteristic of, but not specific for, tuberculous granulomas. A: Foreign-body giant cells have scattered nuclei. B: Langhans cells are not specific for TB. C: Giant cells come from epithelioid macrophages, and foreign-body cells have scattered nuclei. D: Herpes giant cells are infected epithelial cells, not granuloma cells.

questions.stem: Which statement about the causes of granulomatous inflammation is correct?

options.A: Cat-scratch disease is caused by a bacterium
options.B: Crohn disease is listed as an infectious cause
options.C: Mycobacterium leprae is listed as a fungus
options.D: Treponema pallidum is listed as a fungus
options.E: Tumors are not listed as a cause

questions.explanation: Infectious causes are mycobacteria (M. tuberculosis, M. leprae), fungi (Blastomyces, Histoplasma, Coccidioides), Treponema pallidum and the bacterium of cat-scratch disease; Crohn disease and sarcoidosis are unknown/autoimmune causes; reaction to tumors is also listed. B: Crohn disease is under unknown or autoimmune causes. C: M. leprae is a mycobacterium. D: T. pallidum is the bacterium of syphilis. E: Reaction to tumors is listed.

questions.stem: Which pairing of granulomatous cause and its category is correct?

options.C: Sarcoidosis – infectious
options.D: Retained surgical suture – reaction to tumor
options.E: Crohn disease – unknown or autoimmune

questions.explanation: Sarcoidosis and Crohn disease are listed as unknown or autoimmune causes. A: T. pallidum is a bacterium. B: Coccidioides is a fungus. C: Sarcoidosis is unknown or autoimmune. D: Retained material belongs to the foreign-body category.

questions.stem: Which etiology of chronic nonspecific inflammation is listed?

options.A: A single brief thermal burn of the skin
options.B: Rapid elimination of a pyogenic bacterium
options.C: Spontaneous neutrophil apoptosis at the site
options.E: Prolonged exposure to a nondegradable toxin

questions.explanation: Etiologies are persistent infections, repeated bouts of acute inflammation, autoimmune diseases, allergic diseases and prolonged exposure to toxic (nondegradable) agents. A: A single brief injury usually resolves. B: Elimination of the agent leads to resolution. C: Neutrophil apoptosis is part of resolution. D: Transient histamine release is an acute event.

questions.stem: Non-caseating granulomas are mainly encountered in:

options.B: Pyogenic bacterial abscesses of the skin
options.C: Acute viral infections of the skin
options.E: Fibrinous pericarditis after myocardial infarction

questions.explanation: Non-caseating (epithelioid) granulomas are encountered in several chronic inflammatory diseases, especially autoimmune ones; the prototype is sarcoidosis. Caseating granulomas are typical of TB. A: TB typically gives caseating granulomas. B: Abscesses are purulent. C: Acute viral infections give lymphocytic inflammation. E: Fibrinous pericarditis is a fibrinous exudate.

questions.stem: Chronic inflammation develops when:

options.A: The agent is eliminated within hours
options.B: Neutrophils undergo apoptosis at the site
options.C: Lymphatics drain the edema fluid
options.E: The agent persists or cannot be degraded

questions.explanation: Chronic inflammation occurs when the injury is persistent or recurrent, or when the reaction cannot completely degrade the agent (bacteria, tissue debris, foreign bodies). A: Rapid elimination leads to resolution. B: Neutrophil apoptosis is part of resolution. C: Lymphatic drainage is part of resolution. D: Mediator decay is part of resolution.

questions.stem: Besides infectious agents and unknown or autoimmune causes, granulomas also arise from:

options.C: Burns and serous blisters
options.D: Foreign bodies and reactions to tumors
options.E: Parasites and hives

questions.explanation: The four etiology groups are infectious agents, foreign bodies, unknown or autoimmune causes (sarcoidosis, Crohn disease), and reactions to tumors. A: These are not listed granuloma causes. B: Infarction causes acute inflammation. C: Burns cause serous blisters. E: These relate to eosinophils, not granulomas.
